4. Geolocation Data
Geolocation data delivers useful information about citizens’ behavior and movement patterns. Smart cities are already relying on location data for traffic abatement, for decisions about where to locate services and as a means to attract new industries with data-based profiles of markets. For taxpayers, this means better services where they need them. For businesses, it means better resource planning. - Gladys Kong, Near
5. ‘Context Aware’ Computing
Evolving smart cities will require “context aware” computing to better respond to occupants’ needs. This will build upon widely deployed Internet of Things technologies that currently enable centralized command and control. By distributing edge AI capabilities to locally analyze data from multiple sensors, smart cities will be able to react more quickly and accurately to users’ needs and intents. - Vikram Gupta, Synaptics
6. Air Taxis
As smart city technologies evolve, the adoption of air taxis is expected to increase significantly in urban areas. Apart from supporting urban development and the reduction of road congestion, these advanced air mobility solutions can drastically reduce the time required to transport medical supplies, organs for transplant and healthcare professionals to and from isolated areas. - Ketan Anand, Suuchi
7. AI-Powered Public Transit
Are we ready for AI-powered public transportation? This includes dynamically adjusting routes and schedules based on real-time data to minimize wait times and maximize efficiency. Such advancements will improve user engagement with public transit systems, similar to how we monitor viewability patterns and user engagement in social media apps. - Giovanni Punzo, Streann Media
8. Smart Storage
Smart storage that follows you is on the rise. Whether it’s receiving a package you need, having your luggage sent to your destination before you arrive, or the delivery of a hot meal from the local restaurant you love so much, smart storage, with a virtual address that follows you in time and place, is the future. One can envision an NFT-authenticated digital twin being 3D printed at your destination and waiting in storage for you while you’re on your journey. - John Walsh, III, Red Summit
9. Flexible Workspaces And ‘Pilot Labs’
Flexible workspaces and “pilot labs” are on the rise. These facilities help small businesses thrive by taking on the responsibilities of technology, furniture and space. Many of these facilities also come with personnel to aid in coordination, collaboration and mentorship. Urban areas are soon to be flush with affordable, flexible working environments that will empower the SMB space. - Tom Roberto, SG Network Services
10. GenAI-Powered Natural Language Service Models
Driven by the generative AI revolution and large language models, user interfaces for services are evolving, with intuitive interfaces using natural language becoming more common. Smart services provided by machines will increasingly process and even understand natural language, enhancing the user experience. - Gautam Hazari, Sekura.id
11. Proactive Data Security
Smart cities are data-driven; a lot of data flows through various systems and infrastructures. Data security typically is not visible, and users of multiple services are unaware of how insecure systems are until there is a security breach. With AI and autonomous networks, smart cities can be more proactive about detecting, predicting and preventing security breaches and ensuring data security. - Kaitki Agarwal, A5G Networks, Inc.
12. Support For The Gig Economy
Greater access to the gig economy will become an increasingly common convenience in urban areas as smart city technologies evolve. When drivers use mapping apps, for example, they will be able to connect with nearby residents looking for ridesharing services. If someone is stepping out for groceries, they will be able to quickly and easily identify neighbors looking for someone to shop for them. - Anar Mammadov, Senpex Technology
13. Community Health Tracking Systems
Health tracking systems will be expanded and will eventually be able to provide a “disease forecast” that could be used to indicate which areas are more prone to transmission of recurring or novel diseases. Wastewater monitoring became more common after the last pandemic, and the technology could be used for more localized analysis. - Luke Wallace, Bottle Rocket
14. Intelligent Waste Management
Intelligent waste management will soon be common in urban areas. These systems use IoT sensors and AI to monitor waste levels, optimize collection routes and enhance recycling. This reduces fuel consumption, lowers carbon emissions and minimizes landfill use. Efficient sorting and predictive maintenance improve recycling rates and resource conservation, contributing to urban sustainability and environmental protection. - Sri Bhargav Krishna Adusumilli, MindQuest Technology Solutions LLC
15. Automated Public Transit Payment Systems
Automated payment systems are becoming increasingly common among various forms of public transportation in cities. A unified time-based ticket, monthly subscriptions and other ticket types can all be purchased via contactless methods at stops—or even inside vehicles—without the need for a printed ticket or other type of confirmation. - Yuriy Berdnikov, Perpetio
16. Intelligent Traffic Management Systems
As our cities become smarter, we’ll start seeing more intelligent traffic management systems. These systems use real-time data and advanced technology to improve traffic flows, reduce congestion and make public transportation more efficient. - Sarah Choudhary, Ice innovations
17. Integrated Health And Safety Monitoring Platforms
Opt-in, continual and contextualized monitoring platforms that provide an array of services will be offered by both private and public entities. Look for services that monitor current conditions and provide a seamless array of health, safety and green convenience options. Human-aware, properly trained monitoring services will improve the state of today’s urban environments. - James Stanger, CompTIA
18. Smart Parking Systems
The service likely to become increasingly common in urban areas as smart city technologies evolve is smart parking systems. These systems use sensors, cameras and data analytics to provide real-time information on parking space availability. Drivers can use mobile apps to find and reserve available parking spots, reducing the time spent searching for parking and decreasing traffic congestion. - Roman Reznikov, Intellias
19. 24/7 Maintenance Services Carried Out By Robots
In the longer term, I look forward to my local municipality having a small army of AI-driven Boston Dynamics (or similar) robots that can autonomously work night and day to optimize the quality of life for residents by repairing streets, planting trees, building and expanding structures, removing blight and trash, and more. - Sam Glassenberg, Level Ex
20. Micro-Mobility Hubs
As smart city technologies advance, expect to see widespread adoption of urban micro-mobility hubs. These hubs will integrate electric bikes, scooters and car-sharing options, all accessible via a unified digital platform. Enhanced with AI, they’ll offer route optimization, maintenance alerts and availability predictions, streamlining daily commutes and reducing urban congestion and pollution. - Rohit Anabheri, Sakesh Solutions LLC

title: Council Post: How AI Is Taking Over Our Kitchens
text:
Raghav Gupta is CEO at Nymble, where he's transforming how the world eats healthy by building cooking robots for home.
While some people love the work of a kitchen, others can find it grueling and time-consuming. Eating healthy food involves quite a lot of work—meal planning, grocery shopping, cooking and cleanup.
The good news is that kitchens are getting smarter. The Internet of Things (IoT) has firmly gained a foothold in our connected coffee makers and air fryers. Kettles allow us to avoid watching over boiling water, rice cookers and Instant Pots keep us from watching over stoves and microwaves heat food with no input other than setting the time and grabbing it when it is ready.
All these innovations make meal preparation easier. But how will artificial intelligence (AI) transform the way we eat? For over five years, as the founder of Nymble—where we’ve been teaching home robots and AI to cook with the same attention and love as a human—this question has fascinated me. Here’s how I think AI will impact meal planning, grocery shopping and social enjoyment to forever change how we work in our kitchens.
Meal Planning
Decision fatigue, dietary restrictions, lack of variety and getting stuck in the same old routines can quickly make the kitchen seem like a chore.
AI-powered apps make meal planning more manageable by offering personalized suggestions and nutrition advice. For example, Lifesum has been using AI to recognize food items in photos so users can log their food intake with a snap. Similarly, Foodvisor helps you log everything you eat by using image recognition to detect the type of food and the weight of what’s on your plate.
Samsung recently launched its own meal-planning app called Samsung Food, which uses AI to generate instant recipe ideas from photographs of ingredients. Likewise, Yummly, the recipe and meal-planning app, serves up AI-powered recipe recommendations based on the user’s preferences, nutrition goals and lifestyles.
Grocery Shopping
Once you’ve decided what to eat, the work isn’t over. Heading to the grocery store or placing an online order can be a lot of work—do you have any of that specific spice left? Inventory management of the fridge and the pantry is nothing to sneeze at.
Smart refrigerators like Samsung’s Family Hub or LG’s ThinQ track food inventory, suggest recipes based on available ingredients and help you create your next grocery list.
On the retailer side, companies like Walmart are using AI to analyze customer data to identify trends, ensure shelves are always stocked with what customers want and create a better shopping experience.
The Art Of Cooking
Once the meals are planned, the fridge is stocked and the ingredients are ready, it’s time to get to business. While eating is an innate ability, cooking is not. It’s a skill that takes time to build.
Smart appliances like AI-enabled ovens help guide users through recipes with precision, automatically adjusting temperatures and cooking times for optimal results. AI can simulate human-powered cooking by using cameras to look at what’s happening in the cooking process in real time, making decisions like adding ingredients, stirring like a human chef would and understanding what needs to be done next. Appliances like the Chef IQ Mini Oven, or robot chefs like those we create at Nymble, prove that AI can be a private chef.
AI-powered tools can also help people improve their cooking skills. AI-powered chatbots answer questions about cooking techniques and even offer ingredient substitutions.
The future of home cooking blends human creativity with machine precision. AI can help people experiment and explore in the kitchen, giving them the confidence to try new recipes and cooking techniques knowing they have an AI sous chef. But it’s not just about eating to maintain our physical health.
Social Enjoyment
The connection from gathering around a table and sharing food with friends and family nourishes our souls. Casual weeknight dinners, festive holiday feasts or starting the day with a rich breakfast all provide an opportunity to bond and share moments together.
A study from the University of Oxford found that the more often people eat with others, the happier they’re bound to be. Despite this, the majority of people tend to eat their meals alone. Busy schedules and different eating habits can contribute to solitary dining.
AI solutions and cooking tech can reduce the stress and time commitment of cooking, freeing up more time for people to savor one another's company.
The Future Of Kitchens
AI has already revolutionized our culinary world, changing how we approach meal planning, shopping and cooking and giving us extra time. Personalized recommendations that cater to individual tastes and smart appliances that take the guesswork out of cooking have made the kitchen more efficient, enjoyable and accessible to everyone.
However, technology is a tool that serves the consumer. With each consumer being unique, the challenge is to build applications and interfaces that serve each person well.
While millions have been invested in smart kitchen tech, we have yet to see a mass-market implementation of meal planning and grocery shopping that disrupts the space—I’m talking like Amazon for e-commerce or Meta for social. That kind of disruption will succeed by focusing on consumer needs while using breakthrough technology.
For those looking to make their mark on the future of food and tech, here are some things to remember:
• User Experience: Seamless integration into the kitchen is key, enhancing existing processes rather than complicating them. Intuitive interfaces, time-saving features and personalized recommendations will add value.
• Embrace The Data: Understanding what consumers want—and what they don’t—is the difference between making it and not.
• Collaborate And Create: Tue innovations in food and tech will come from chefs, engineers, nutritionists, data scientists and other experts.
It’s an exciting time for entrepreneurs, technologists and inventors to innovate. By developing new tools that empower individuals to take control of their health and well-being through food, we can use AI to help us transform our kitchens, making delicious, nutritious and personalized meals more accessible to all.

title: Council Post: Smart Hospitals: Combining Data Management, AI Tools And Compliance
text:
Alexandr Khomich, President & CEO at Andersen.
Thanks to digital solutions, the healthcare industry has made immense progress over the last few decades. In a not-so-distant future, the state of things will be even more exciting. A smartwatch could detect an anomaly in a person’s heart rate—and in a matter of minutes, an AI-powered system at their hospital would analyze the data, cross-reference it with their medical history and schedule a consultation with a cardiologist.
The promise of artificial intelligence for hospitals is indeed huge. However, as modern healthcare facilities transition to “smart” ones, how do we balance innovation with patient safety and compliance?
The Rise Of Smart Hospitals
Once prioritizing disease treatment, healthcare is now primarily focused on disease prevention. This requires constant monitoring of patients’ health and effective data management, from EHR data to information gathered from wearables. Consequently, the volume of data is increasing rapidly, which leads to the adoption of various digital tools—data management systems, AI, robotics, the IoT and many more—by hospitals and clinics. All this has brought to life the concept of a smart hospital.
Such facilities are currently on the rise. According to Research and Markets, in 2023, the smart hospitals market made up $57.53 billion. By 2030, it is expected to reach $187.20 billion. Statista figures also prove this exponential growth—from $35.9 billion in 2021 to an impressive $83 billion in 2026.
But what exactly are smart hospitals? While there’s no universal definition, these facilities prioritize the digitization of information flows, seamless interoperability between systems and a future-proof technology infrastructure—these are the key features McKinsey highlights. They are present in such institutions as Mayo Clinic, Cleveland Clinic, Massachusetts General Hospital and others that are topping the smart clinic rankings in 2024.
Complexities Of Building A Smart Hospital Ecosystem
According to Alena Burdzialouskaya, Head of Partnerships and Digital Health Solutions at Andersen, “The transition from a good hospital to a good smart hospital is a task of enormous complexity.” She addressed this at a recent webinar we held in 2024. The infrastructure must be built and maintained, AI solutions and other digital tools must be implemented into clinical workflows smoothly, patient safety must be ensured, and hospital staff must be trained. All this is an uphill battle many healthcare systems still grapple with.
At its core, a smart hospital runs on a centralized data platform ingesting, processing and analyzing information from countless sources—EHRs, medical imaging, IoT devices and more. Machine learning models and AI applications then extract insights to guide care delivery.
But integration is key. EMRs, hospital information systems, wearables and other data pipelines must adhere to interoperability standards. Such tech maturity demands the engagement of IT experts, that’s why leading smart hospitals employ numerous tech personnel or have their own big innovation teams.
For instance, one of Europe’s largest university hospitals, an example mentioned in our webinar, employs approximately 1,200 specialists in administration and management. This is about 5.5% of the entire staff. Many of them are directly involved in making this hospital smart and maintaining the interconnected ecosystem.
Of course, clinicians also contribute to building smart facilities with their hands-on knowledge and expertise, which ensures that AI products fully align with medical realities. External IT vendors, in turn, give hospitals access to specialized capabilities for remote monitoring, telemedicine and custom software development.
Smart Hospitals: Where Regulatory Issues Hide
As smart hospitals grow and introduce new solutions, they must handle complex regulations around data privacy, cybersecurity and patient safety. HIPAA compliance is a table stake, but healthcare facilities also need robust frameworks for obtaining explicit patient consent for using de-identified data to train AI models.
Preventing unauthorized access and minimizing the risk of re-identification are vital. So is ensuring AI-generated clinical recommendations are unbiased and explainable. Clear guidelines must define liability when AI outputs contradict human clinician judgement.
There are also compliance requirements for medical devices and wearables underpinning smart hospitals. Risk classifications, approval mechanisms and data integrity requirements get stricter as these tools increase in complexity and risk level. Biomedical labs also face stringent CLIA, CAP and quality control standards governing data handling and interoperability.
The Evolving Regulatory Paradigm For AI In Healthcare
But herein lies the core challenge—existing regulatory frameworks aren't designed for the constant evolution of AI and machine learning algorithms. These self-learning models can change dramatically through continuous retraining cycles.
So, ensuring patient safety while introducing new AI products is getting truly challenging. How can smart clinics achieve this? There are no easy answers, but in any case, this must be done through cross-disciplinary collaboration. Healthcare providers, tech companies, regulatory bodies and ethics boards must unite forces to introduce regulatory frameworks that consider AI's iterative nature. Transparency, ongoing monitoring and proactive risk management should be priorities.
Responsible AI Implementation: An Action Plan
Smart hospitals can't afford missteps when developing and deploying intelligent medical solutions. Based on years of experience building clinical systems, Andersen's experts have developed a strategy for successful implementation of AI in a compliant medical device. It can also be used for other AI-related initiatives within smart hospitals:
• Assemble cross-functional teams spanning healthcare, AI, regulatory and domain experts.
• Conduct thorough requirements gathering anchored in clinical workflows.
• Make regulatory compliance a nonnegotiable priority throughout the AI life cycle.
• Maintain open communication with regulators, providers and ethics boards.
• Integrate robust cybersecurity and data governance protocols.
• Perform rigorous testing, validation and ongoing model monitoring.
• Document comprehensively to facilitate audits.
• Incorporate continuous end-user feedback.
• Embed AI performance tracking into DevOps processes.
• Invest in extensive clinician training on AI's impacts.
By taking a systematic approach that prioritizes compliance, safety and human-centered design, healthcare facilities can unlock AI's potential while maintaining trust.
Conclusion
AI's potential for smart clinics is staggering. However, implementing initiatives in this field requires a thoughtful approach and governance.
There are still numerous technical, ethical and change management obstacles to overcome. But for health-tech leaders, the stakes have never been higher—or the opportunity bigger—to positively impact millions of lives through safe and responsible AI innovation.

title: Council Post: The Inevitability Of Our Dependence On AI Agents In Investing
text:

These advanced tools, which autonomously interpret data, make decisions and execute actions when prompted in natural language, will play a pivotal role in streamlining investment decision-making and mitigating risks for investors.
Reliance on AI agents is not just a possibility, but an inevitability as this decade of increasing uncertainty progresses. At RAFA.AI, I provide teams of AI agents to help individual investors make better investing decisions. I've seen a dramatic improvement in investment efficiency and risk mitigation when investors use AI agents. During our research phase, we interviewed many individual investors, as well as wealth managers, and it became obvious to me that these AI agents will have a profound effect on the entire financial services industry.
State Of Brokerages In 2024
The online brokerage industry has grown substantially in the last decade. However, this growth has recently plateaued and is now flat, with decreases in customer satisfaction and trust.
Despite ubiquitous access to trading interfaces, trust levels have remained flat across significant segments of investors, particularly DIY investors and younger demographics such as Millennials and Generation-Z, according to J.D. Power’s 2024 U.S. Self-Directed Investor Satisfaction Study.
The challenge of differentiation compounds this lack of trust. Despite their best efforts, many online brokerages struggle to attract and retain clients, with differentiated offerings in a highly competitive market, which has led to unsustainable customer acquisition efforts like zero-fee trading, percentage incentives and bonuses based on commissions and performance. This race to the bottom jeopardizes many brokerages' sustainability.
Increasing Demand For Personalized Services
Despite the growth of self-service platforms, from what I've seen in the industry, there is a rising demand for personalized financial advice. This is not a fleeting trend but a fundamental shift in investor behavior, especially by traditional DIY investors.
This demand for personalized services is a call to action for the industry to adapt and evolve. Investors now expect more than just a standard, one-size-fits-all trading interface; they seek services that align with their specific financial objectives and situations. It’s a need that AI agents are uniquely positioned to fulfill.
AI Agents Deliver Personalized, Quantifiable Value
AI agents have emerged as transformative tools in the financial sector, offering significant, measurable benefits to both individual investors and institutional investors. They excel at providing real-time, tailored intelligence and guidance at scale, a task that traditional financial advisors find impossible because of their high-cost structures and one-size-fits-all services.
The value of AI agents is particularly evident when market conditions can change rapidly, and the window for timely decision-making is often narrow. AI agents can help mitigate potential financial risks and maximize returns. This capability allows investors to stay ahead of market trends and adjust strategies quickly, ensuring they maintain a favorable position.
Furthermore, AI-driven insights and recommendations are delivered with a level of speed and accuracy that surpasses human ability, empowering brokerage firms to enhance their service offerings and improve overall client satisfaction. They streamline complex investment processes and increase financial access.
The Future For Investors
Looking ahead, the brokerage industry is on the cusp of a deeper integration of AI technologies to meet the growing demand for personalized investment strategies and risk management solutions. Investors increasingly recognize the benefits of AI, and they now expect brokerage services, which rely on trade volume, to incorporate these advanced technologies as part of their standard offerings.
Brokerages that successfully integrate AI agents into their service models stand to gain a significant competitive edge. By offering personalized, intelligent and responsive services, they can improve customer satisfaction and trust, reduce churn, increase revenues and attract a broader base of clients. The potential benefits of integrating AI technologies into brokerage services are immense, and firms that recognize this stand to reap substantial rewards.
Here are some best practices for successfully integrating AI agents into your business:
1. Make sure that education is a key component of user onboarding. AI agents are powerful tools that have many features that users may not have time to discover on their own. Remember that seamless onboarding is key to educating and retaining users.
2. If you are an online brokerage, AI agents are an additional layer of value you can offer to your brokerage clients with minimal disruption of user experience. When starting to introduce AI agents, the less you can interrupt the user experience, the better. With AI agents, you can deliver more value to the user in a hyper-personalized way, reduce user churn and increase customer lifetime value.
3. If you are a wealth manager, integrating AI agents into your workflow should start with personalized customer-facing communications, reports, etc. This will help make the most impact on your clients from the get-go.
Conclusion
As the financial landscape continues to evolve, the dependence on AI agents within the brokerage industry becomes not just an advantage but a certainty. The integration of AI offers a promising path forward for both brokerages and investors, transforming challenges into opportunities and setting new standards for financial services in the digital age.
